chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.
chapter_note: This chapter is front-loaded with Christian overlay: Gospel proof-texting of the two trees (¶1–3, ¶10) and NT narrative exempla (Judas/Paul; ¶7–9). The oldest teaching substrate appears mainly in the middle and second half as systematic correspondential exposition: the “good tree”/“bad tree” each having five limbs (intellectual qualities) mapped to cosmic beings/ships/realms (¶11–12, ¶15, ¶17–19, ¶22–24). Two clear editorial/institutional grafts cross the cosmos→institution boundary by identifying “taste” and salvific process with the “holy church,” teachers, catechumens, and alms (¶13, ¶16), and another applies the “bad fruits” taste to “sects” (¶20). Several paragraphs are mixed where a basically cosmological mapping has had sect/church phrases inserted (notably ¶15, ¶22, ¶24).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Sets the parable within a Jesus-and-disciples scene; this enters via Gospel tradition rather than the internal cosmological system.
Explicit Gospel citation formula (“As it is written in the Gospel…”) and quoted saying; by definition a later Christian overlay layer.
Continues petition + “it is written… scriptures,” i.e., proof-text framing rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Discusses how ‘sects’ interpret the parable; polemical/intra-community positioning rather than cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: because [ ... ] tree, as it grows on this composite earth, [ ... ] date palm, because [ ... ], for not absolutely every part of the date palm is used!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic/dialogue frame attribution (“Then speaks our master Manichaios, the apostle of greatness, to his disciples.”) and surrounding sect-polemic scaffolding; retained the underlying correspondential illustration about a tree on the composite earth (mixture within a single natural form).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a late dialogue-title frame and sectarian polemic, but preserves an older natural-correspondential argument about mixture in composite nature (tree/date-palm example) used to explain why composite beings are not absolutely one-sided.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] their child, as it strikes [ ... ] while first one [ ... ] in them [ ... ] at the end there is one [ ... ] it occurs in its fibres and its branches [ ... ] There is a bad dust in them [ ... ] date palm [ ... ] before the tree that [ ... ] bad; because they give the decision [ ... ] the one that they name [ ... ] the type [ ... ] name it: tree [ ... ] is sweet [ ... ] writing [ ... ] they shall establish [ ... ] man [ ... ] it is sweet [ ... ] seed of the [ ... ] and it is used for their nourishment [ ... ] will explain [ ... ] may not join to the [ ... ] mankind, as they are named [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, process-style exposition using a natural exemplar (fibres/branches/dust/seed) to describe mixture; no citation, no church-institution identifiers.
NT narrative exemplar (Judas; “Satan entered him… handed the saviour… Jews… wood/cross”); enters via Christian tradition.
Continues Judas Iscariot exemplar; Christian narrative overlay.
Paul persecution/conversion exemplar (“persecutor… church of God…”); even if used to argue ‘mingling,’ the entry vector is NT biography.
Introduces the ‘saviour preached’ parable and urges listening; this is a Christian overlay bridge into Mani’s exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how I will reveal to you [ ... ] the expound[er ... ] the trees [ ... ] the Father [ ... ] all of them, as he [ ... ] in the [ ... ] world [ ... ] this good tree, the [ ... ] the light of this good tree [ ... ] the Pillar [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins internal cosmological identification of the ‘good tree’ with Light-system realities (Father, Pillar, Light), shifting from citation to system description.

paragraphs.core_text: ... the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [ ... ] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological mechanics (light elements mingled/compounded; ‘intellectuals’ on the tree’s body) with no institutional application.
Editorial seam into institution: identifies ‘taste’ as the ‘holy church… teachers… catechumens,’ a cosmos→community mapping (flagged extension).

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, this is the good tree [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Deictic summary within the teaching sequence; no citation or institutional cross-mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [ ... ] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening revelatory address fragments (“[ ... ] I reveal to you [ ... ]”) and removed the institutional insertion “Its consideration is the holy church.” The retained list preserves the cosmos→cosmos mapping of intellectual limbs to Pillar/Perfect Man, First Man (ship of living waters), Third Ambassador (ship of living fire), and the Father (aeons of Light).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core correspondential structure (five intellectual limbs mapped to named cosmic beings and ships) is present, but one limb has been editorially redirected to the institutional ‘holy church,’ which breaks the internal-system mapping rule.
Institutional/cultic graft: catechumens, alms, purification in the holy church; cosmos→church application rather than cosmological mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: It is consideration that shall [ ... ] they shall be raised up [ ... ] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic degree-ascent mapping (consideration→counsel→insight→thought→mind) aligned with cosmic stations (First Man/ships/night-day/Father). Internal cosmic architecture dominates.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the good tree that shall give good fruit, [ ... ] is the entire life and light for ever [ ... ] occurs [ ... ] ever, it is blessed [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concludes the good-tree teaching in cosmological terms (life/light forever) without institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] bad [ ... ] happen in [ ... ] from [ ... ] also [ ... ] the way that it is [ ... ] the good tree [ ... ] of the fire [ ... ] they are the ruling-power [ ... ] heaven and the wheel [ ... ] they are the five fleshes that walk [ ... ] fruit [ ... te]aching as of error, the mystery that [ ... wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns to internal mythic mechanics (ruling-power, heaven/wheel, five fleshes; Satan as cosmic agent). Though polemical language (“error”) appears, the paragraph still reads as system description.
Defines ‘taste’ as contemporary ‘sects… teachers… law after law’; this is explicit cosmos→social-institution identification.
Summarizes via appeal to ‘scriptures’ and ‘our master’; functions as proof-text/recognition claim (“all the sects know it”), suggesting a later scripturalizing layer in this parable-based chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... I will] reveal to you and you [ ... ] The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death. Its counsel is transmigration [ ... ] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [ ... ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [ ... ] vessel. Its mind is the [ ... ] the lump, the last bond, the [ ... ], they that Satan cast away [ ... ] the great [ ... ] and they fall [ ... ] the Darkness [ ... ] all [ ... ] and they take away [ ... ] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [ ... ] the fruit of Darkness, the one that they [ ... ] for ever and ever [ ... ] his face [ ... ] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the sectarian insertion in the first limb definition (“from which the sects take instruction”), which crosses from cosmic principle (‘law of death’) to contemporary group identification.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core negative parallel to the five-limb ascent: a structured descent mapping into transmigration, furnaces/gehenna/smoke, vessel, and the final lump/bond in Darkness. A small editorial sect-reference is embedded in the first limb.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you, which you [ ... ] to it [ ... ] good fruit [ ... ] its fruit bad [ ... ] in it, in its existent days [ ... ] in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Wrap-up of the bad-tree exposition; despite second-person rhetoric, it does not pivot into church rules or Gospel citation and stays within the explanatory register.

paragraphs.core_text: it being changed from [ ... ] which lies in its good earth [ ... life] and light; as death and Darkness do not exist [ ... ] Also, the bad tree is Matter [ ... ] [ ... wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [ ... ] Darkness and death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed application/affective address and exhortation markers (“Concerning this… my beloved ones… them in truth,”) and removed the self-referential gloss (“I understand it alone…”) to leave the underlying dualistic identification (good earth = life/light without death/Darkness; bad tree = Matter in bad earth with Darkness/death).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying core dualist ontology is present (Matter vs life/light; death/Darkness exclusion), but the paragraph is wrapped with audience-address/application voice that likely reflects editorial or homiletic delivery.
Beatitude-style exhortation (“Blessed is every one… separates them…”). Though consistent with dualism, it is applied to the hearer’s capability rather than expounding the system.
Conditional exhortation about separating principles leading to ascent/fall; application to the hearer rather than system mapping.
Concluding beatitude/confession-like line (“Blessed is whoever can believe!”); hortatory closure rather than cosmological exposition.
